new_assertions.title: edge-local flip position is gauge-dependent
new_assertions.body: The repair-surviving route pair has odd relative sheet parity in both the stored gauge and an independently reconstructed exact-state lexicographic gauge, but the unique delta-1 edge moves from stored edge 2710 to edge 2724. Therefore no particular edge position is an invariant location of the oddness.

new_assertions.title: nonzero fundamental-basis cycle count is basis-dependent
new_assertions.body: On the same repaired 5x4 representation carrier, seven valid deterministic spanning orders yield nonzero fundamental-basis syndrome counts 22, 28, 32, 35, or 115 while preserving non-exactness. Therefore the count is not an intrinsic obstruction magnitude.

new_assertions.title: stored labelled-sheet distinction is not literal-future distinction
new_assertions.body: All six stored binary sheet pairs in the witness have distinct recursive canonical-frame action-token class IDs but identical complete no-canonicalization literal-action future trees. Thus stored class distinction does not imply distinct literal future behavior.
new_assertions.scope: all six groups of repair-surviving witness

new_assertions.title: witness binary fiber collapses at behavior resolution
new_assertions.body: Replacing stored sheet identity by independently computed complete literal-action future behavior collapses each of the six two-sheet witness fibers to one class, leaving no two-sheet carrier on which the stored witness deltas can act.

new_assertions.title: canonical slots are not fixed physical columns
new_assertions.body: Only identity and horizontal reflection preserve the fixed 5x4 Connect4 winning-line hypergraph, yet 10 of 14 witness canonicalizer uses employ other column permutations and every displayed witness state contains at least one residual not lying on a physical winning line in that displayed frame. Therefore a canonical slot is a local abstract action slot unless a transporter maps it back to a physical frame.

new_assertions.title: route endpoint reconvergence is relation-dependent
new_assertions.body: In one common source frame the two routes end at different exact states in different arbitrary-column residual orbits with different literal-action future trees, but a global action relabeling makes their future trees coincide and their action-unlabelled multiset/set futures coincide. Hence reconvergence is true only under a named behavioral/action-relabel relation, not unqualified equality.
new_assertions.scope: both start-sheet realizations of surviving witness

new_assertions.title: support-release closure has narrower exact meaning
new_assertions.body: For all 56 residual occurrences in witness states, support-release/turn-capacity agrees with exhaustive alternating-turn/gravity feasibility of each residual considered in isolation; this does not establish full-game realizability with first-win stopping or competing residuals.

new_assertions.title: representation-graph non-exactness survives independent recomputation
new_assertions.body: Independent component, cycle-rank, potential-consistency, parity-reachability and gauge checks reproduce cycle rank 542, non-exactness, and the unique directed opposite-parity source-target pair on the repaired 5x4 edge carrier. Thus the representation-graph obstruction is not explained by a simple arithmetic, cycle-enumeration, or parity-convention error.

support_refinements.refinement: Use 'recursive canonical-frame action-token class' for the audited implementation unless transporter-aware recursive label alignment is explicitly included.
Always name the relation: exact state, physical symmetry, arbitrary-column orbit, fixed-frame literal future, global-action-transporter future, multiset/set future, or stored base quotient.
By default in this campaign, mean 'non-exact Z2 cochain on the declared representation carrier'; do not silently upgrade to physical/game-state obstruction.
Attach the chosen fundamental-cycle basis/order. Treat existence/non-exactness as invariant; treat the count as basis-relative.
